title: The Mineral Chameleon: Potassium Permanganate
subject: Chemistry
objective: Potassium permanganate is made by fusing pyrolusite (MnO₂) with KOH and an oxidiser to give dark green potassium manganate (Mn +6). In neutral or acidic water manganate disproportionates (3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O), the 'mineral chameleon' Glauber saw; commercially it is oxidised at an anode. In acid MnO₄⁻ takes 5 electrons to give almost colourless Mn²⁺ (so it is its own indicator in titrations); in neutral or faintly alkaline solution it takes 3 electrons and gives brown MnO₂.

short.q: Describe the preparation of KMnO₄ from pyrolusite with equations.
short.solution: 2MnO₂ + 4KOH + O₂ → 2K₂MnO₄ + 2H₂O (green manganate); then 3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O, or commercially electrolytic oxidation MnO₄²⁻ → MnO₄⁻ + e⁻.

short.q: Write the half-reactions of permanganate in acidic and neutral media.
short.solution: Acid: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (E° = 1.52 V). Neutral / faintly alkaline: MnO₄⁻ + 2H₂O + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ + 4OH⁻ (E° = 0.59 V).
